blocks.text: Blockchain 2.0 adds features beyond cryptocurrency: smart contracts, decentralized applications (dApps) and better scalability. Smart contracts are self-executing contracts whose terms are written in code; in real estate one can transfer ownership to the buyer and funds to the seller automatically once payment and ownership checks are complete.

blocks.prompt: What does Blockchain 2.0 introduce beyond basic cryptocurrency (MCQ 10)? Describe Blockchain 2.0 and its features (long question 6).
blocks.explanation: (b) decentralized applications and smart contracts. Blockchain 1.0 mainly recorded currency transfers; Blockchain 2.0, as on Ethereum, runs programs on the chain. Smart contracts enforce agreements automatically (property sales, insurance payouts); dApps are applications whose logic runs on the blockchain rather than one company's server; and improved scalability lets more transactions be processed. These bring blockchain into finance, supply chains, real estate and insurance.

items: Blockchain 2.0: smart contracts, dApps, better scalability (property transfer example).
